raw_confidence: mean(assessor_confidence, verifier_confidence), x0.5 if the verifier disagrees
interval: Wilson score, 95%, one unit per (item, tranche)
caveats: Reference set is small (40 gold items, one model); tranche estimates are coarse.

Both runs score the same items, so predictions are not independent. Counts, the n >= 10 rule and the Wilson intervals therefore use one unit per (item, tranche) -- an item that was right in one run and wrong in the other counts as 0.5 -- instead of one per prediction.
Wilson intervals on fractional counts are an approximation, and tranche membership is itself estimated from the same data: treat them as indicative.
Calibration quality (ECE) is measured by 5-fold cross-validation grouped by item; predictions whose tranche has < 10 training items are not calibrated and go to human review.
Valid only for the model named here on this corpus (TS 38.331 v19.3.0 extract); re-run calibrate.py after any model, prompt or retrieval change.
Intervals capture sampling noise only, not systematic error shared by the LLM judges.
